human_owner.summary: Approved in advance by the owner through auto mode; the Claude reviewer decides.

non_blocking_findings.finding: The cable pulls the pinned upper arm toward shoulder flexion, so the muscles resisting that pull are shoulder extensors (latissimus, teres major, posterior deltoid). shoulder_position_hold credits mainly the clavicular deltoid (0.35), a shoulder flexor, and no lat or teres major activity appears. This is a modelling approximation under the existing demand vocabulary, not a material error for an isolation elbow-extension exercise.
non_blocking_findings.suggested_correction: A future revision could add glenohumeral_joint/extension with emphasis assist and sides working to credit the lats and teres major holding the upper arm.

non_blocking_findings.finding: postural_stabilization spreads low-coefficient stabilizer credit across both legs and the trunk. This is plausible for an upright standing cable exercise, and it is a general tracer pattern rather than a definition error.

The frames show one standing pose and do not show which arm works, but the instructions specify the right hand and the same-side repetition on the other arm, so unilateral with the right side working is reasonable.

model_reviewer.summary: The definition matches the source. It is a standing single-arm high-pulley triceps pushdown with a supinated grip and the upper arm pinned at the side. The only moving joint is the elbow, which extends against the cable. Elbow extension as the sole working-side primary action correctly yields the three triceps heads as primaries and the anconeus as a synergist. Unilateral laterality with one_sided_limbs ["arm"] keeps the unloaded arm at zero. Grip and wrist_stability fit a handle held in the hand, shoulder_position_hold fits the pinned upper arm, and postural_stabilization fits the upright stance. The open_chain and elbow_extension labels are appropriate. The remaining concerns are minor and non-blocking.
